subject: Nanotechnology
title: Active Targeting with Antibodies
description: Learn Active Targeting with Antibodies in one minute.

hook.text: Glue an antibody onto a nanoparticle and it homes in on cancer cells like a guided missile.

buildup.text: Antibodies bind to receptors overexpressed on tumor cells — pulling the nanoparticle to the right address.

discovery.text: Antibody-drug conjugates already work — Kadcyla targets HER2-positive breast cancer with precision.

twist.text: Antibodies are large and expensive — small peptides and aptamers are being tested as cheaper alternatives.

climax.text: Over a dozen antibody-drug conjugates are now FDA-approved — active targeting has become clinical reality.

punchline.text: An antibody turns a nanoparticle into a guided missile.

quiz.question: How do antibody-decorated nanoparticles target tumors?
options: Antibodies dissolve tumor cells on contact
Antibodies bind to receptors overexpressed on tumor cells, concentrating the particle there
Antibodies block blood flow to the tumor
